items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: He lugged it all the way up to Minton’s and he recorded us, the Tony Scott Quartet.

ctx.x: Jerome Richardson, Gigi Gryce, one weekend it was Miles. And that rhythm section, that’s the best I ever had anything to do with. Those two people were — now on Tony’s first record we did — well the first one — well I’m going to back up a little bit. I wish they’d reissue those records. One night up at Minton’s the first time we were there with the three, a guy who I befriended named Johnny Mandel, who was one of these guys, he played jazz bass trumpet and he used to write arrangements for Elliot Lawrence and all…
